1. Scientific Analysis

Analysis Type

Dark Au sphere sizing: log_blob_detect seeds (counting/sanity) + run_sam_analysis instance masks (primary sizing via regionprops equivalent_diameter, no radius clamp), seed->instance matching, sigma-derived fallback for recall misses, mask-edge border exclusion. Watershed documented fallback.

Interpretation

The sample is a densely packed monolayer of spherical Au nanoparticles imaged by TEM at 300 kV (pixel size 0.396 nm from field-of-view calibration). The primary size distribution was built from 111 seed-matched, non-border SAM instances using regionprops equivalent_diameter with no radius clamp, i.e. the diameter of a circle with the same projected area as each particle's segmented mask. This is a physically meaningful outer (particle-to-background) boundary measurement. The distribution is strongly unimodal and sharply peaked: median 74.6 nm, mean 74.3 nm, with a very tight IQR of ~1.4 nm and the bulk of counts in two adjacent bins spanning ~73-76 nm. This indicates a highly monodisperse population — consistent with a well-controlled synthesis of nominal 80 nm spheres. The measured median sits ~7% below the 80 nm nominal outer diameter; two independent estimators bracket the truth from below (SAM equivalent_diameter 74.6 nm at the outer boundary; sigma-derived LoG cross-check 70.4 nm, which tracks the darker particle core and is expected to read smaller). The consistency of these two independent methods (6% apart, both single-mode) supports that the true outer diameter is ~75-80 nm and the population is genuinely narrow. Shape metrics reinforce the sphere interpretation: median solidity 0.993 and median circularity 0.90, with a tight cluster in the QC scatter (most particles at solidity ~0.992-0.994, diameter ~73-76 nm); the handful of low-solidity/low-circularity outliers at 59-63 nm are the small tail likely from partially occluded or under-segmented particles rather than a true second size mode. There is no evidence of over-segmentation (no cluster of fragments below ~1/4 of typical area; smallest areas ~17.5k px vs typical ~28k px, i.e. >0.6x, and only 5 particles below the main peak). Detection is robust: 117 LoG seeds and 155 SAM instances, with 111 matched, only 2 under-segmented (multi-seed) and 4 recall-misses handled by sigma fallback (3% fallback fraction). The main caveat for the size measurement is that the reported IQR (~1.4 nm) is almost certainly narrower than the true polydispersity, because 44 of 159 objects (28%) touching the mask edge were excluded and the tight two-bin peak may be compressed by the equivalent_diameter estimator on dense, mutually-contacting particles.

Original Image
Analysis Visualization

3. Scientific Claims

Claim 1: The Au nanoparticle population is highly monodisperse, with a unimodal equivalent-diameter distribution centered at a median of 74.6 nm (mean 74.3 nm, IQR ~1.4 nm), approximately 7% below the 80 nm nominal outer diameter and corroborated by an independent sigma-derived cross-check at 70.4 nm.

Scientific Impact: A tight, single-mode size distribution confirms well-controlled synthesis and provides a quantitative outer-boundary size for these ~75-80 nm Au spheres, which directly governs their optical (plasmonic) and assembly behavior; the two independent estimators agreeing within 6% strengthens confidence in the reported size.

Literature Search Query: Has anyone quantified the monodispersity of nominally 80 nm Au nanospheres by TEM and found the measured outer-boundary median to fall systematically ~7% below the nominal diameter?

Keywords: gold nanoparticles, monodispersity, size distribution, TEM, equivalent diameter, plasmonic nanospheres

4. Caveats & Limitations

The reported IQR (~1.4 nm) is almost certainly narrower than the true polydispersity: 28% of objects (44/159) touching the mask edge were excluded, biasing toward interior, cleanly-separated particles, and the equivalent_diameter estimator on densely-contacting spheres can compress the apparent spread. Both size estimators read below the 80 nm nominal (SAM 74.6 nm outer boundary; sigma 70.4 nm core-tracking), so the absolute value carries a ~7-12% negative bias whose origin (segmentation under-call at contact boundaries vs. true undersize vs. nominal-value uncertainty) is not resolved. Shape-based QC metrics were reporting-only and not used for exclusion (avoiding clean-subset bias). Particle count (115 interior) carries ~20% uncertainty. The sigma cross-check is not independent ground truth in the strict sense — it is a second detector on the same image.
